summary: The general term for cryolipolysis for localised fat concerns.
leadAnswer: Fat freezing (cryolipolysis) uses controlled cooling to target localised fat in specific areas, and is not a weight-loss treatment. Whether a given area can be treated at all depends on whether an applicator can draw and hold it, which is something a doctor checks in person.
seoTitle: Fat Freezing Malaysia | Cryolipolysis Treatment | Kaiteki

routes.title: A pinchable pocket that diet has not shifted
routes.body: Controlled cooling applied to a defined pocket of fat that can be pinched and drawn into an applicator.

routes.title: A defined pocket of fat under the chin
routes.body: Relevant only where the fullness under the chin is genuinely fat.

variantModule.heading: Cooltech or CoolSculpting: which device, and why
variantModule.intro: Both are cryolipolysis devices working on the same principle. They differ in applicator design.

items.title: Cooltech
items.body: The manufacturer describes 360° cooling around the drawn-in tissue rather than from one contact plate, and more than one applicator can run at once, so two areas or both flanks may be treated in one appointment.

items.title: CoolSculpting
items.body: An applicator draws the target area against a cooling plate.

ctaMid.heading: Not sure whether your area is one an applicator can hold?
ctaMid.body: A doctor can check in person, with a pinch test, whether the area is fat an applicator can treat.

sessionSteps.title: Consultation and assessment
sessionSteps.body: The doctor checks whether the fat in the area can be drawn into an applicator.

sessionSteps.title: Preparation
sessionSteps.body: The treatment area is marked, and a protective gel pad and applicator are positioned over the pocket of fat.

sessionSteps.title: The cooling cycle
sessionSteps.body: The area is cooled for a set period. There is an initial period of intense cold and a firm pulling sensation from the suction, which commonly eases as the area becomes numb.

sessionSteps.title: Afterwards
sessionSteps.body: The applicator is removed and the area is massaged.

bands.title: Straight afterwards
bands.body: The area often looks red and feels firm, cold or oddly numb, and this typically settles over the following hours to days.

bands.title: The first weeks
bands.body: Temporary tenderness, swelling, tingling or a dull ache in the treated area can persist for a few days to a couple of weeks, and some people find loose clothing or a compression garment more comfortable during that period.

afterSession.aftercare: Keep to a stable weight with your usual diet and activity.

risks.common: Redness, swelling, bruising, firmness, numbness, tingling, itching or cramping in the treated area, and altered skin sensation that may take some weeks to normalise.
risks.lessCommon: Lingering pain in the treated area, and paradoxical adipose hyperplasia, in which the treated fat pocket firms and enlarges rather than reduces.
risks.pigmentNote: It acts on fat below the skin, not on pigment, so skin tone matters less than it does with lasers. The thickness and distribution of fat in the area matter more.
cannotDo: It is not a weight-loss treatment, not a treatment for obesity, and not a substitute for diet, exercise or medical weight management.
Not every pocket of fat is one an applicator can draw and hold.
It does not stop remaining fat cells enlarging with weight gain, which is why a stable weight matters.
risks.disclose: Tell your doctor about anything in the list under who should postpone or avoid it, and about any implant, device or medication.

sections.heading: What is fat freezing?
body: Fat freezing is the everyday name for cryolipolysis, a non-surgical approach that uses controlled cooling to target pockets of fat in specific areas of the body.

sections.heading: Why does cooling affect fat and not the skin around it?
body: Cryolipolysis is based on the idea that fat cells are more sensitive to cold than the surrounding skin, nerves and muscle. During a session, an applicator cools a defined area to a controlled low temperature for a set period.
The aim is to affect fat cells within the treated pocket while limiting the effect on nearby tissue.

faqs.q: Is fat freezing a weight-loss treatment?
faqs.a: No. It targets localised pockets of fat in specific areas, not overall body weight, and is intended for people at or near a stable weight.
Most people feel intense cold and a firm pulling from the suction at the start, which usually eases as the area goes numb.

faqs.q: How many sessions will I need?
faqs.a: It depends on the area, the amount of localised fat and how you respond.

faqs.q: When might I notice a change?
faqs.a: Any change is gradual, because the body clears the treated cells over several weeks, so it is usually assessed a couple of months after the session.
